$comment: Benchmark data for the charts on diarist.dev/models/. Every number is copied from the file named in each block's `from` field; the website build fails if this file is missing or malformed. Published numbers are from leaderboards cited in docs/04; measured numbers are from docs/eval on the machine below.

diarization_published.source: VoiceArena Diarization-Bench v1, 139 English conversations, collar 0, overlap scored

asr_published.metric: average WER, percent, lower is better

rows.note: experimental in Diarist, off by default
at 1.1 s latency; Diarist's default for English
not on the leaderboard yet; measured below

asr_measured.from: docs/eval/2026-10-16-shipped_en.md and docs/eval/2026-10-16-shipped_n35.md (cpWER column of the transcript attribution tables); session names, minutes and groups from docs/05-eval-data.md and the same tables; the per-model summary is in docs/04-model-guide.md, section 3
asr_measured.source: docs/eval, 16 Oct 2026, the shipped 0.1.0-beta.2 configuration (file lookahead 1.12 s, diarizer offline geometry)

sessions.name: AMI ES2002a
sessions.group: public AMI meeting, far-field mix, word-level reference

asr_measured.note: The Zoom sessions are the author's own meetings; their references are Zoom's machine transcripts with per-participant speaker labels, so cpWER there mixes recognition disagreement with attribution. AMI ES2002a has a hand-made word-level reference. The in-room stress session (Aug 14) is left out: its reference hides several people behind shared room devices, so its cpWER (43.9 and 42.9) measures the reference, not the models. 0.1.0-beta.1's setting (docs/eval/2026-10-16-nemotron_en.md and -nemotron35.md) scored 10.3, 8.5, 5.1, 7.8, 7.1 and 19.8 (EN) and 12.0, 9.2, 5.4, 7.9, 7.3 and 23.0 (Nemotron 3.5) on the same sessions.

vram_measured.source: measured on the RTX 3080, excluding the desktop's own 1.5 GB

rows.scenario: Live recording, idle (Nemotron 3.5 and the diarizer resident)
rows.note: the EN model sits at 1.18 GB

rows.scenario: Live recording, two sessions (microphone and system audio)
rows.note: spikes of 0.5 to 0.6 GB per session; the app budgets 2 GB

speed_measured.from: docs/eval/2026-10-16-shipped_n35.md and docs/eval/2026-10-16-shipped_en.md (GPU wall time: 324 minutes of audio in 10.6 and 10.9 minutes, 30.6 and 29.9 times real time, including a standalone diarization pass the app does not run; the speech pass alone 78 and 76 times), summarised in docs/04-model-guide.md, section 3 and README.md (What it does); live first text about 0.2 s from docs/research/08-runtime-cli-contract.md, section 7

languages_measured.from: docs/eval/2026-10-16-fleurs.md (rows n35_rc_13, the file setting, and en_rc_13 for the EN model; card column) and docs/04-model-guide.md, section 6
languages_measured.source: FLEURS test split (CC-BY-4.0), about 10 minutes per language (37 to 55 sentences joined with 1.5 s of silence), transcribed by Diarist's runtime at the file setting (lookahead 1.12 s) without diarization
languages_measured.metric: WER, percent (CER for Japanese), lower is better

en_model_english.note: the EN model on the same English slice; nearly all errors are dropped quiet recordings (36 of 55 peak below -30 dBFS)

languages_measured.note: Smoke tests on small slices: one or two points either way is noise. The model card's numbers use the full test split and NVIDIA's normaliser; FLEURS writes numbers as digits and the runtime, with no normalisation grammars, writes them as words, so these numbers sit 1 to 9.5 points above the card's, least for English and most for Hindi and Japanese. Automatic detection picks es-ES and pt-PT for the Latin American and Brazilian slices.
